  2. thm✓Lax919488.RefinementBounds

    Bounded twin-width refinement of triangulations

    Every generalized triangulation of a ddd-manifold MMM with nnn top-dimensional simplices has a refinement of MMM whose dual multigraph has twin-width at most 444. For d≥1d\ge1d≥1 and n≥2n\ge2n≥2, its size is O(dnlog⁡2n)O(dn\log_2 n)O(dnlog2​n). The proof constructs the refinement for any finite face pairing, so MMM can be any space homeomorphic to its realization.

    22/-- Theorem 1 with the explicit refinement from equation (1). -/
    23axiom bounded_twin_width_refinement {d n m : ℕ} (T : Diagram d (Fin n) (Fin m))
    24 {M : Type} [TopologicalSpace M] (h : T.IsPairing) (realizes : Nonempty (T.Realization ≃ₜ M)) :
    25 let s := depth d n
    26 let U := refine T s
    27 let N := Fintype.card (Cell (Fin n) (Fin m) s)
    28 U.IsPairing ∧ U.Refines T ∧ Nonempty (U.Realization ≃ₜ M) ∧
    29 N ≤ n + (d+1)*n*layers n ∧
    30 (1 ≤ d → 2 ≤ n → (N : ℝ) ≤ 7 * d * n * Real.logb 2 n) ∧ WidthAtMost U 4

  3. lem✓Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth

    Twin-width of a dual multigraph

    The initial black multiplicity between two cells counts the face gluings joining them, including loops. When two parts merge, each surviving part has a black edge to the new part if it had a black edge to both old parts. It has no edge if it had no edge to either. Every other case gives one red edge. Edges between surviving parts keep their multiplicities. The width is the maximum red degree, counting red edges with multiplicity.

    A contraction sequence for the simple adjacency graph lifts to a sequence of the same width for the dual multigraph.

    1import Lax919488.FacePairings
    2import Lax228581.TwinWidth
    3
    … module docstring, 15 lines
    19
    20namespace Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth
    21
    22open FacePairings Lax228581.TwinWidth
    23
    24noncomputable section
    25
    26def edgeMultiplicity {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype E] (T : Diagram d V E) (u v : V) : ℕ := by
    27 classical
    28 exact (Finset.univ.filter fun e =>
    29 ∃ b, (T.side e b).cell = u ∧ (T.side e (!b)).cell = v).card
    30
    31structure Entry where
    32 black : ℕ
    33 red : ℕ
    34 deriving DecidableEq
    35
    36def combine (a b : Entry) : Entry :=
    37 if 0 < a.black ∧ 0 < b.black then ⟨1,0⟩
    38 else if a = ⟨0,0⟩ ∧ b = ⟨0,0⟩ then ⟨0,0⟩ else ⟨0,1⟩
    39
    40structure ContractionSequence {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
    41 (T : Diagram d V E) (k : ℕ) where
    42 steps : ℕ
    43 parts : ℕ → Finset (Finset V)
    44 edges : ℕ → Finset V → Finset V → Entry
    45 symmetric : ∀ i A B, edges i A B = edges i B A
    46 initial : parts 0 = singletonPartition V
    47 initialEdges : ∀ u v, edges 0 {u} {v} = ⟨edgeMultiplicity T u v,0⟩
    48 final : (parts steps).card ≤ 1
    49 merge : ∀ i < steps, ∃ A ∈ parts i, ∃ B ∈ parts i, A ≠ B ∧
    50 let rest := ((parts i).erase A).erase B
    51 let C := A ∪ B
    52 parts (i+1) = insert C rest ∧ edges (i+1) C C = ⟨0,0⟩ ∧
    53 (∀ D ∈ rest, edges (i+1) C D = combine (edges i A D) (edges i B D)) ∧
    54 ∀ D ∈ rest, ∀ F ∈ rest, edges (i+1) D F = edges i D F
    55 width : ∀ i ≤ steps, ∀ A ∈ parts i, ∑ B ∈ parts i, (edges i A B).red ≤ k
    56
    57def WidthAtMost {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
    58 (T : Diagram d V E) (k : ℕ) : Prop := Nonempty (ContractionSequence T k)
    59
    60axiom lift_sequence {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} [Fintype V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V]
    61 (T : Diagram d V E) {k : ℕ} (h : HasTwinWidthAtMost T.dual k) : WidthAtMost T k
    62
    63end
    64end Lax919488.MultigraphTwinWidth

  4. defLax919488.FacePairings

    Generalized triangulations and their dual graphs

    Take finitely many copies of the standard ddd-simplex. Each gluing identifies two distinct facet occurrences by a permutation of their vertices. A facet occurs in at most one gluing. Unpaired facets give boundary, and two facets of the same simplex may be paired. The realization carries the quotient topology. The dual multigraph has one vertex per simplex and one edge per gluing. Its adjacency relation on distinct vertices records the support of the black edges used in a contraction sequence.

    1import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.StdSimplex
    2import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
    3import Mathlib.Topology.Constructions.SumProd
    4
    … module docstring, 13 lines
    18
    19namespace Lax919488.FacePairings
    20
    21abbrev Corner (d : ℕ) := Fin (d+1)
    22abbrev Simplex (d : ℕ) := stdSimplex ℝ (Corner d)
    23
    24/-- A side of a gluing. Its frame sends the reference facet opposite 0
    25to the chosen facet of the cell. -/
    26structure Side (d : ℕ) (V : Type) where
    27 cell : V
    28 frame : Equiv.Perm (Corner d)
    29
    30def Side.port {d : ℕ} {V : Type} (s : Side d V) := (s.cell, s.frame 0)
    31
    32/-- The two sides of each gluing are indexed by false and true. -/
    33structure Diagram (d : ℕ) (V E : Type) where
    34 side : E → Bool → Side d V
    35
    36def Diagram.IsPairing {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) : Prop :=
    37 Function.Injective fun p : E × Bool => (T.side p.1 p.2).port
    38
    39/-- Reindex the barycentric coordinates by a vertex permutation. -/
    40def reindex {d : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Corner d)) (x : Simplex d) : Simplex d :=
    41 ⟨fun i => x.val (σ.symm i), fun _ => x.property.1 _, (σ.symm.sum_comp _).trans x.property.2⟩
    42
    43inductive Diagram.Gluing {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) :
    44 (V × Simplex d) → (V × Simplex d) → Prop
    45 | face (e : E) (x : Simplex d) (onFace : x.val 0 = 0) :
    46 T.Gluing ((T.side e false).cell, reindex (T.side e false).frame x)
    47 ((T.side e true).cell, reindex (T.side e true).frame x)
    48
    49/-- The quotient of the disjoint union of closed geometric simplices. -/
    50abbrev Diagram.Realization {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) := Quot T.Gluing
    51
    52instance {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) : TopologicalSpace T.Realization :=
    53 letI : TopologicalSpace V := ⊥
    54 inferInstanceAs (TopologicalSpace (Quot T.Gluing))
    55
    56def Diagram.chart {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) (v : V) (x : Simplex d) :
    57 T.Realization := Quot.mk _ (v,x)
    58
    59def Diagram.dual {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) : SimpleGraph V where
    60 Adj u v := u ≠ v ∧ ∃ e b, (T.side e b).cell = u ∧ (T.side e (!b)).cell = v
    61 symm := by
    62 constructor
    63 rintro u v ⟨ne,e,b,hu,hv⟩
    64 exact ⟨ne.symm,e,!b,hv,by simpa using hu⟩
    65 loopless := ⟨fun _ h => h.1 rfl⟩
    66
    67/-- A homeomorphism of realizations under which every new characteristic
    68map embeds into a model simplex of the original triangulation. -/
    69def Diagram.Refines {d : ℕ} {V E W F : Type} (U : Diagram d W F) (T : Diagram d V E) : Prop :=
    70 ∃ h : U.Realization ≃ₜ T.Realization, ∀ w, ∃ v, ∃ f : C(Simplex d, Simplex d),
    71 Topology.IsClosedEmbedding f ∧ ∀ x, h (U.chart w x) = T.chart v (f x)
    72
    73end Lax919488.FacePairings

  5. defLax919488.StackedPillows

    Stacked pillow refinement

    Insert sss pillows at each face gluing. Each pillow consists of two ddd-simplices paired along the ddd facets containing vertex 000. Their opposite facets attach to their two neighbors. Seam jjj is the gluing after the first jjj pillows. The two end seams use the frames of the old gluing. With s=0s=0s=0 the construction recovers the original face pairings.

    1import Lax919488.FacePairings
    2import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
    3
    … module docstring, 11 lines
    15
    16namespace Lax919488.StackedPillows
    17
    18open FacePairings
    19
    20abbrev Cell (V E : Type) (s : ℕ) := V ⊕ (E × Fin (2*s))
    21abbrev Joint (d : ℕ) (E : Type) (s : ℕ) := E × (Fin (s+1) ⊕ (Fin s × Fin d))
    22
    23def leftHalf {s : ℕ} (j : Fin s) : Fin (2*s) := ⟨2*j.val, by omega⟩
    24def rightHalf {s : ℕ} (j : Fin s) : Fin (2*s) := ⟨2*j.val+1, by omega⟩
    25
    26def originalSide {d s : ℕ} {V E : Type} (a : Side d V) : Side d (Cell V E s) :=
    27 ⟨.inl a.cell, a.frame⟩
    28
    29def seam {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) (s : ℕ) (e : E) (j : Fin (s+1)) :
    30 Bool → Side d (Cell V E s)
    31 | false => if h : j.val = 0 then originalSide (T.side e false)
    32 else ⟨.inr (e,rightHalf ⟨j.val-1,by omega⟩), 1⟩
    33 | true => if h : j.val < s then ⟨.inr (e,leftHalf ⟨j.val,h⟩), 1⟩
    34 else originalSide (T.side e true)
    35
    36def refine {d : ℕ} {V E : Type} (T : Diagram d V E) (s : ℕ) :
    37 Diagram d (Cell V E s) (Joint d E s) where
    38 side
    39 | (e,.inl j), b => seam T s e j b
    40 | (e,.inr (j,i)), b =>
    41 ⟨.inr (e, if b then rightHalf j else leftHalf j), Equiv.swap 0 i.succ⟩
    42
    43/-- The number of pillows in equation (1), truncated at zero. -/
    44def layers (n : ℕ) := 2 * Nat.clog 2 n - 1
    45
    46/-- A zero-dimensional triangulation needs no pillows. -/
    47def depth (d n : ℕ) := if d = 0 then 0 else layers n
    48
    49/-- The shorter stacks used for the leading constant in the abstract. -/
    50def shortLayers (d n : ℕ) := if d ≤ 1 ∨ n ≤ 5 then 0 else Nat.clog 2 n
    51
    52end Lax919488.StackedPillows
    53
  6. lem✓Lax919488.PillowSubdivision

    Realization of the stacked pillow refinement

    In positive dimension, inserting any finite stack of pillows at every gluing preserves the quotient space. Under the homeomorphism, each new simplex embeds as a closed subset of an original model simplex. The empty stack works in every dimension.

  7. lem✓Lax919488.RefinementSize

    Size of the refinement

    With nnn simplices and mmm face gluings, inserting sss pillows at each gluing gives n+2smn+2smn+2sm simplices. Counting facet occurrences gives 2m≤(d+1)n2m\le(d+1)n2m≤(d+1)n. For d≥1d\ge1d≥1 and n≥2n\ge2n≥2, the resulting bound in equation (2) is at most 7dnlog⁡2n7dn\log_2 n7dnlog2​n. With the shorter stacks the estimate improves to 2dnlog⁡2n2dn\log_2 n2dnlog2​n, with dual twin-width at most 444.

  8. lem✓Lax919488.RefinedDual

    Contraction sequence for the refined dual graph

    Replace each dual edge by the path through its pillow simplices. The underlying simple graph has a contraction sequence of width at most 444 when the stack has 2⌈log⁡2n⌉−12\lceil\log_2 n\rceil-12⌈log2​n⌉−1 pillows. For n≤1n\le1n≤1 or d=0d=0d=0, the trivial refinement suffices. Zipping the two vertices of each pillow directly onto the tree gives the same bound with the shorter stacks.

    no assumptions

    →
    lem✓Lax919488.RefinedDual (1st statement)

    Process the subdivided dual edges one at a time. Place the original vertices at leaves of a binary heap and move the interior vertices of each path up the source branch and down the target branch. At every intermediate partition a tree node has at most 3 tree neighbors and 1 extra neighbor on the current path. Finally contract the tree from the leaves inward.
